item.research_question: Can binary phase diagrams be used to predict the phase formation (single solid solution, mixed phases, or intermetallics) of high entropy alloys (HEAs) through a phenomenological method combined with machine learning?
item.material_system: 614 reported HEAs (Level 3) and 42 newly synthesized complex compositions containing 4 to 7 elements from refractory metals, transition metals, and main group elements (e.g., Al2CoCrCuNi)
item.processing_route: Suction casting of master ingots (arc-melted 3 times in high purity argon, 99.7 wt% purity elements) into 3 mm diameter rods; annealing at temperatures > 0.7 Tm for some database entries; phase formation temperature (Tpf) optimized at 0.8 Tm for as-cast alloys
item.test_conditions: X-Ray Diffraction (XRD) analysis using Cu Kα radiation; Machine Learning classification using Random Forest with 300 trees and 2-10 fold cross-validation on 614 HEAs; validation on 42 new compositions
key_findings: The model achieved an overall HEA prediction success rate above 80% and a single-phase HEA prediction rate above 80%.
Validation on 42 randomly selected complex compositions yielded a success rate of 81% (34 out of 42 predicted correctly).
Level 1 (disordered phases) single phase predictions had success rates of 89–90% for as-cast HEAs.
Level 2 (including B2 + SS) overall and B2 + SS phase prediction success rates were near 85%.
Level 3 (including IM+ phases) overall success rate was 80%, with IM+ phase prediction rates of 73–78%.
High accuracy was maintained even with training set percentages as low as 50%.
The optimized phase formation temperature (Tpf) for as-cast HEAs was determined to be 0.8 Tm.
item.mechanism: The authors hypothesize that HEA structural stability is encoded within binary phase diagrams; they use phase field percentages at a specific temperature (Tpf) and a phase separation parameter (PSP) to quantify the tendency of constituent binary pairs to form specific phases, which are then combined combinatorially to predict multi-component alloy phases.
item.limitations: The study excludes minor phases such as line compounds; mechanically alloyed HEAs are not included because ball milling tends to retain metastable phases; the model's performance slightly abates when annealed HEAs are added to the as-cast set.
item.future_work: The authors propose including additional physical parameters (e.g., mixing enthalpy) into the ML to improve accuracy, and interacting with other models like CALPHAD where the current model serves as a fast screening tool for in-depth thermodynamic studies.
quotes: For the first time, a phenomenological method analysing binary phase diagrams to predict HEA phases is presented.
Out of the 42 HEAs, 34 were predicted by ML correctly, yielding a success rate of 81%.

The phenomenological method is built on the hypothesis that the constituent binary alloys encode a wealth of information about the multi-component alloy in terms of crystal structures, elemental mixing, and phase separation.
